Date: 2026-03-04 17:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Asha Patel (CEO), Ethan Chen (CTO), Maya Rodriguez (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Head Product), Priya Singh (VP Sales), Jordan Lee (Head of People), plus ~150 team members
Location: Zoom / All-Hands
Recording: Yes (auto-transcript)
transcript:
[00:00] Asha (CEO): Hey everyone, happy to see so many faces, um, thanks for joining. We'll kick off the Q1 all-hands — quick agenda: metrics, product, hiring, security, then Q&A.

[00:28] Asha: Quick housekeeping — recording is live, please keep questions for the end if you can or drop them in chat. Also we'll share the deck after.

[00:45] Ethan (CTO): Alright, I'll start with a brief infra update. We're seeing steady improvements in tail latency after the 2.1 runtime change, although a few tenants still saw small regressions with long seq models. We're tracking that — the KV cache path had an interaction with the new batching heuristics, so Maya and infra are on it.

[01:15] Maya (VP Eng): Yeah, to add — there was a latency blip on Tuesday where requests with persistent KV caches and long context lengths increased P99 by about 10%. We rolled a mitigation within 6 hours but we need a deeper fix; the root cause looks like an edge case in the continuous-batching window where the kernel selection favored a quantized path which doesn't play nice with the client's prompt patterns. It's subtle.

[01:48] Asha: Great — please make sure to put a short summary in #incidents and the postmortem. Folks, reliability is top priority this quarter especially as we push Dedicated to more beta customers.

[02:10] Liam (Head Product): On product, quick overview: Hosted API improvements — streaming UX polish, function/tool calling stability, and some prompt templating helpers. Dedicated: beta is live with two customers with reserved capacity; biggest asks have been autoscale policies and easier billing visibility. Private: we've shipped the initial VPC control-plane prototype and are working on HSM/KMS integrations.

[02:45] Priya (VP Sales): From Sales — pipeline is healthy. We're seeing expansion motion from a couple of AI-native startups and two enterprise accounts asking about Dedicated and air-gapped Private options for EU data residency. Pricing questions keep coming up around committed vs burst capacity.

[03:10] Audience (chat): "Can you share numbers behind 'healthy pipeline'?"

[03:20] Priya: Sure — without disclosing deal names here, pipeline $ ARR coverage is about 4.2x target for the quarter; conversion velocity slowed slightly in Feb due to procurement cycles but we're optimistic. I'll circulate a sanitized deck.

[03:48] Asha: On overall company metrics — revenue growth is trending per plan. Net expansion helped offset a small decrease in new logo velocity. We closed the Series C last year and runway is solid; go-to-market spend needs to be smart this year.

[04:15] Jordan (Head People): Hiring update — we've onboarded 18 new folks in the quarter, mainly infra and SRE. Priorities next quarter: finish hiring for Dedicated infra, two SEs for enterprise support, and ux/product folks for developer experience. We're opening a hiring prioritization doc and want team leads to rank reqs by March 10.

[04:45] Asha: A couple strategic notes — 1) investment in Dedicated and Private will be the focus for mid-market/enterprise growth, 2) we need to be surgical on where we spend for GTM, and 3) engineering time should be aligned to SLAs and remove blockers that prevent sales wins.

[05:10] Ethan: On the technical roadmap — major milestones this quarter: release 2.2 runtime with kernel scheduler improvements, autoscaling policy UI for Dedicated, and a Private control-plane hardened for SOC 2/ISO audits. The 2.2 release includes changes to kernel selection heuristics to avoid the regression Maya mentioned. We also plan a perf benchmark public doc.

[05:46] Maya: Ops/infra tasks: increasing internal chaos-testing of our fallback routing, more end-to-end tests for private deployments, and improving our preflight checks for customer onprem installs. We're also tightening observability around token-level latency so we can pinpoint regressions faster.

[06:15] Liam: Roadmap details — short-term focus is "reliability and enterprise readiness": A) Dedicated autoscale and billing transparency B) Private control plane + KMS C) Improve developer ergonomics for streaming and function calling. Longer term: better model routing by policy, multi-model orchestration, and cost-aware batching suggestions in the Console.

[06:50] Audience question: "Will Dedicated customers be able to choose quantization profiles?"

[07:00] Maya: Yes — the plan is to surface quantization profiles and recommended settings per model workload. We'll also provide guardrails to avoid quality regressions. We want to make it safe for customers to choose aggressive quantization where appropriate.

[07:20] Priya: Shout-out — the AE team ran two pilots last month that highlighted the need for clearer docs on trade-offs between Dedicated and Hosted; we'll be working with Product to make a one-pager and a matrix.

[07:40] Ethan: Security update — our SOC 2 readiness work is on track. We've completed about 70% of the control matrix and a third-party assessor is scheduled for late Q2. For Private: KMS integration work is planned and will include customer-managed keys and HSM support later this year.

[08:10] Asha: We're hearing more from customers about audit logs and SSO requirements — please prioritize SAML/SCIM and session logging for the Console.

[08:30] Jordan: People reminder — performance review cycle starts next month; calibrations are scheduled for April 2–9. Also, we'll run a company-wide engagement pulse next week, please respond.

[08:50] Asha: Ok we'll open the floor to Q&A. Please unmute or use the q/a.

[09:05] Q1 - Anonymous (Engineering): Are we still planning to open-source any of the runtime components?

[09:15] Ethan: Short answer: selective open-source. We plan to open some tooling and benchmarking code to help community adoption, but core high-throughput runtime will remain productized; we need to protect IP and product-market fit. We will publish reproducible benchmark harnesses.

[09:40] Q2 - Sales (live): Pricing ask — can we be more flexible on trial limits for startups that show rapid usage?

[09:50] Priya: We're piloting flexible trial bands for strategic startups — AE can request exceptions. We just need to balance risk/revenue and fraud protection.

[10:05] Q3 - Support: We saw an uptick in support tickets around model hallucination and inference cost spikes. Any plan?

[10:15] Liam: For hallucination QAs we'll invest in evals tied to customer prompt sets and add monitoring alerts if quality drifts. For cost spikes, the Optimizer tooling will push recommendations — batching, prefix caching, and quantization profiles. Please file examples to help us tune suggestions.

[10:40] Asha: A few tactical items — 1) Engineering: please prioritize the KV cache fix and postmortem, 2) Product: produce the Dedicated vs Private decision matrix, 3) Sales: share pricing clarifications and churn analysis with the AE team. We'll set owners and due dates.

[11:05] Maya: I'll own the kernel heuristic follow-up; we'll target a patch release in two weeks and a full 2.2 rollout mid-quarter.

[11:20] Priya: I'll collect the pricing asks and send an updated band to the AE team by next Wednesday, and share a sanitized slide for GTM.

[11:35] Jordan: I'll publish the hiring prioritization doc and ask managers to rank by March 10.

[11:50] Audience (chat): "Can we get a short doc about how to position Dedicated vs Hosted for customers?"

[12:00] Liam: Yes, we'll produce a positioning one-pager and an external-facing FAQ. Expected by March 11.

[12:15] Asha: Before we close — culture note: shout-out to infra and support teams for handling the incidents and to recruiting for the new hires. We're in a growth phase but must keep engineering focus on reliability and customer success.

[12:40] Audience (live): quick comments and applause.

[12:55] Asha: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck, the postmortem summary, and the action items in the next 48 hours. If you have urgent questions, please ping leadership or your manager.

[13:10] Ethan: Quick final reminder — please run the new local perf harness if you're on infra and add any flaky tests to the backlog.

[13:30] End of recording: meeting closed.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript with a few mis-hearings ("KV cash" in one snippet, "onprem" sometimes transcribed as "on prem"), speaker overlap occasionally labeled as 'Audience' or 'Q1 - Anonymous'.
